figures.caption: Peak current delivered into the cell, sinking and sourcing, over 200 process-and-mismatch samples. The two distributions overlap almost completely: mean source/sink imbalance is \SI{6.4}{\percent}. Absolute drive falls short: \SI{23.0}{\micro\ampere} sourcing and \SI{24.4}{\micro\ampere} sinking against a \SI{33}{\micro\ampere} target, reached by 2 of 400 measurements. Roughly \SI{1}{\volt} of headroom is left unused at each rail (Table~\ref{tab:ctrlamp-mc-celldrive}), so the limit is current, not swing.

Input-referred offset. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}: die-to-die spread, not the within-die channel-to-channel term, for which no mismatch-only run of this design exists. The distribution is Gaussian with \(\sigma = \SI{4.82}{\milli\volt}\) against a \(\sigma \leq \SI{2}{\milli\volt}\) budget; 37 of 200 samples fall inside the \(\pm\SI{1}{\milli\volt}\) rules shown, which are the limits entered on the test. Offset lands directly on the commanded electrode potential and is the dominant accuracy term at low cell current.

Phase margin driving the \SI{10}{\pico\farad} test load. A cell load adds resistive loading that lowers the loop gain and raises the margin (Table~\ref{tab:ctrlamp-cell-loop}). 171 of 200 samples meet the \SI{60}{\degree} design target: \SI{85.5}{\percent} per channel, \SI{53.4}{\percent} across four. Minimum sample \SI{59.3}{\degree}.

Slew rate on both edges of a \SI{1}{\volt} step into \SI{10}{\pico\farad}. Rising and falling averages are \SI{1.74}{\volt\per\micro\second} and \SI{1.65}{\volt\per\micro\second}, a \SI{5}{\percent} imbalance: the tail current is steered into one input device and mirrored to the output, so the slewing current is equal in both directions by construction.

Supply current of the local bias generator over 200 process-and-mismatch samples, with the \texttt{tt} corner at the same trim code marked. Monte Carlo gives \(\sigma/\mu = \SI{12.5}{\percent}\), \(17.7\)--\SI{33.1}{\micro\ampere}, where the five process corners span \SI{1.2}{\percent}, \(23.25\)--\SI{23.52}{\micro\ampere} (Table~\ref{tab:biasgen-dcop}, interpolated to \texttt{BiasAdj}~=~37); the corner sweep is at \SI{27}{\celsius} against \SI{37}{\celsius} here, which accounts for the \SI{0.45}{\micro\ampere} of mean offset and not for the width. A self-biased loop fixes its current by a device-ratio and resistor balance that a global corner shift leaves intact but local mismatch does not, so corner analysis under-reports this term tenfold. It is the largest single contributor to A1's own spread (peak cell current \SI{14.5}{\percent}, \(f_{\mathrm{u}}\) \SI{12.4}{\percent}), leaving roughly \SI{7}{\percent} in quadrature for the amplifier's own devices. This is a separate netlist and a separate draw, so sample \(n\) here is not sample \(n\) in the A1 tests and the two must not be paired.

tables.caption: Offset statistics. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, \texttt{BiasAdj}~=~37, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling. The distribution is Gaussian, so mean $\pm\,3\sigma$ is meaningful here and is not quoted for the clipped quantities in the tables that follow. Spec and yield are the \(\pm\SI{1}{\milli\volt}\) limits entered on the test, the fraction of uncalibrated channels within \(\pm\SI{1}{\milli\volt}\); the \(\sigma \leq \SI{2}{\milli\volt}\) design budget is a separate criterion and is also missed, by \num{2.4}$\times$. This run varies process as well as mismatch, so \(\sigma\) is die-to-die and is an upper bound on the within-die channel-to-channel offset that the four-channel column assumes; a \texttt{castalia\_mm\_25} re-run is needed to separate the two.

Cell-drive statistics with the amplifier loaded by the Randles cell. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling. $I_{\mathrm{SRC}}$ and $I_{\mathrm{SNK}}$ carry the \SI{33}{\micro\ampere} rev-2 target and yield \SI{0}{\percent} and \SI{1}{\percent}: the topology is symmetric but under-sized. The headroom rows show why: close to \SI{1}{\volt} is left between $V_{\mathrm{CE}}$ and each rail when the current limit is hit, so swing is not the constraint. Regulation error is negligible at zero current and reaches \SI{-48}{\milli\volt} at \SI{10}{\micro\ampere}, set by the low loop gain available once the cell loads the output node.

Small-signal stability driving the \SI{10}{\pico\farad} test load. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling. Percentiles and worst case are quoted rather than \(\pm 3\sigma\) for the margins, which are not normally distributed.

Output-referred noise in unity-gain feedback, amplifier and local bias generator together. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling. Noise analysis \SI{0.1}{\hertz}--\SI{100}{\mega\hertz}, 20 points/decade. Integrated noise is \SI{24.7}{\micro\volt} rms, about \SI{50}{\percent} higher than the folded-cascode amplifier because the output current mirrors contribute noise that the folded cascode did not have; this is the cost of the symmetric drive. It remains roughly 100 times below the \SI{2.441}{\milli\volt} ADC LSB, so the amplifier is not the noise-limiting element in the channel. \SI{37}{\percent} of the noise power lies below \SI{10}{\hertz}, leaving the measurement band flicker-dominated.

Large-signal response, \SI{1}{\volt} step into \SI{10}{\pico\farad}. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling. No numeric limit is defined for slew rate, settling or overshoot. Both edges settle to \SI{0.1}{\percent} within about \SI{1}{\micro\second} with no long tail, in contrast to the folded cascode, whose falling edge reached \SI{91}{\micro\second} at the 99th percentile. Overshoot is larger on the falling edge (\SI{4.4}{\percent}) than the rising (\SI{0.94}{\percent}) and is consistent with the \SI{60}{\degree} phase margin.

Local bias generator operating point, shared by all four channels. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling. The four rails hold their wide-swing relationship in every sample: $V_{\mathrm{BNC}} = V_{\mathrm{BNM}} + V_{\mathrm{ov,n}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{BPM}} = V_{\mathrm{BPC}} + V_{\mathrm{ov,p}}$. Supply-current spread of \SI{12.5}{\percent} propagates to the drive and slew distributions above. Because the block is shared, this term is common-mode across the four channels: it does not average out between them, and it cancels in channel-to-channel differences.
